name: SHT30-DIS-B10KS
title: SHT3x-DIS (SHT30, SHT31, SHT35): digital humidity and temperature sensor, I2C, 2.5 mm DFN-8
summary: A calibrated relative-humidity and temperature sensor that reports linearised 16-bit readings over I2C at up to 1 MHz, with CRC on every word and two selectable addresses (0x44, 0x45). It runs from 2.15 V to 5.5 V, idles at 0.2 µA in single shot mode and also offers periodic acquisition, an alert output, a reset pin and an on-chip heater. The three grades differ only in accuracy: SHT30 ±2 %RH and ±0.2 °C typ, SHT31 ±2 %RH and ±0.2 °C over a wider span, SHT35 ±1.5 %RH and ±0.1 °C. The package is an open-cavity 2.5 mm × 2.5 mm × 0.9 mm DFN-8.
key_figures: ±0.2 °C typ, 0 °C to 65 °C (SHT30); ±0.2 °C typ, 0 °C to 90 °C (SHT31); ±0.1 °C typ, 20 °C to 60 °C (SHT35)
0.2 µA typ idle (single shot); 600 µA typ measuring; 1.7 µA average at 1 reading/s

notes: All are tape and reel; the quantity is parts per reel. The grades share pins, package and interface and differ in RH and temperature accuracy.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: I2C data line, bidirectional. Needs an external pull-up.

pins.name: ADDR
pins.function: Address select: low gives 0x44, high gives 0x45. Must be tied to a logic level, never left open.

pins.name: ALERT
pins.function: Goes high when an alert condition is met. Leave unconnected when not used.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: I2C clock line; the sensor holds it low during clock stretching. Needs an external pull-up.

pins.name: VDD
pins.function: Supply, 2.15 V to 5.5 V. Decouple with 100 nF next to the pin.

pins.name: nRESET
pins.function: Active-low reset with an internal pull-up to VDD (50 kΩ typ). Leave open when unused, or tie to VDD through 2 kΩ or more.

pins.name: R
pins.function: No electrical function. Connect to VSS.

pins.name: PAD
pins.function: Centre (die) pad on the underside, tied to VSS inside. Soldered to the board for mechanical strength; a triangular notch marks the pin-1 corner.

tables.title: Humidity sensor specification (Table 1)
notes: Typical and maximum accuracy tolerance are defined in Sensirion's Humidity Sensor Specification Statement.

Repeatability is three standard deviations (3σ) of repeated back-to-back readings under steady conditions, a figure for the noise on the output; the low, medium and high settings are the three measurement modes.
Specified range: the span over which the specification holds. The extended range is the full 0 to 100 %RH; the normal range for best performance is under Recommended operating condition.
Response time: time to reach 63 % of a step in humidity, at 25 °C with 1 m/s air flow. In a product it depends on how the sensor is mounted. With ART enabled it is shorter by a factor of 2.
Long-term drift is typical for use inside the normal RH/T range; the maximum is < 0.5 %RH/yr. Solvent vapours and outgassing from tapes, adhesives or packaging can raise it.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit (Figure 11)
circuits.description: The sensor on an I2C bus. VDD is decoupled to ground by 100 nF at the pin; SCL and SDA each have a pull-up RP to VDD and run out to the bus master. ADDR is grounded, so the address is 0x44. VSS, the centre pad and pin R all go to ground. nRESET and ALERT run out to the host and may be left open.

operation.text: One chip carries a humidity element and a temperature element feeding one shared ADC, plus calibration memory, linearisation and processing, alert logic, a power-on reset and the I2C interface. Readings leave the part already calibrated, linearised and corrected for temperature and supply voltage.

Best performance is within 5 °C to 60 °C and 20 %RH to 80 %RH. Long stays outside this window, high humidity above all, can shift the RH reading for a while (about +3 %RH after 60 h above 80 %RH); back inside the window it drifts back to calibration unaided. Long exposure to extremes can speed ageing. Sensirion's SHT handling instructions apply in storage, assembly and use.
VDD is decoupled by a 100 nF capacitor placed as close to the sensor as possible. The supply may move no faster than 20 V/ms within its range or the part may reset.

SCL and SDA are open-drain with diodes to VDD and VSS, and every device on the bus only pulls low; external pull-ups (10 kΩ, for example) bring the lines high, sized for the bus capacitance and clock rate. The clock runs anywhere from 0 to 1000 kHz; up to 400 kHz the bus follows I2C Fast Mode. Clock stretching is supported and is chosen per command.

ADDR low gives address 0x44, ADDR high gives 0x45; the pin is never left floating. It can be switched while running, as long as its level holds from START to the end of the transfer. Giving each sensor its own ADDR line and switching them lets more than two sensors share one bus.

ALERT can drive a microcontroller interrupt input. It reflects the RH and T readings against programmable limits, set as described in a separate application note, and goes high when an alert condition is met. Current drawn from it heats the sensor; driving only a transistor gate or base avoids that. Leave it open when unused.
Pulling nRESET low for at least 1 µs resets the part much like a power cycle. It has an internal 50 kΩ (typ) pull-up to VDD; when unused it is left open or tied to VDD through 2 kΩ or more.
The centre pad is connected to VSS inside, so its wiring is free electrically; it is soldered to the board for mechanical reasons. The SHTxx/STSxx design guide covers design-in.

When VDD passes VPOR the part starts up and becomes idle after tPU, ready for commands. Whenever it is neither measuring nor talking it drops to idle by itself to save power; idle cannot be commanded.

Each transfer opens with START and closes with STOP. Commands are 16 bits and already carry a 3-bit CRC. Every 16-bit data word sent or received is followed by an 8-bit CRC. On writes the checksum must be sent, as the part ignores data without a correct one; on reads the master may check it or not. After any command the part needs at least 1 ms before it accepts the next.

The master sends the write header and a 16-bit measurement command; the sensor acknowledges each byte by pulling SDA low after the 8th SCL falling edge and starts converting on the command's acknowledge. Each command gives one temperature and one humidity result. The repeatability setting (low, medium, high) trades measurement time and energy against noise.

After the conversion the master sends START and a read header. The sensor returns two temperature bytes and a CRC, then two humidity bytes and a CRC, continuing only while each byte is acknowledged; the master ends with NACK and STOP. A NACK after any byte stops the transfer early, so a master that skips the checksums can read temperature with its CRC and humidity without, then NACK.

With a no-stretch command, a read header sent before data is ready is answered with NACK. With a stretch command, the sensor acknowledges the read header and holds SCL low until the conversion is finished, then releases it and sends the result.

One periodic command starts a continuous series of temperature and humidity pairs at 0.5, 1, 2, 4 or 10 measurements per second, at the chosen repeatability; clock stretching is not available in this mode. Rate and repeatability set the current drawn. Results are read with Fetch Data (0xE000); if no new result is waiting the read header gets a NACK and the transfer ends, and each fetch empties the result memory. A measurement command sent while a measurement is under way is best preceded by Break.

ART (accelerated response time), command 0x2B32, runs periodic acquisition at 4 Hz. It is started, read and stopped like any other periodic command. Sensirion's EK-H5 evaluation kit can demonstrate it.
Break (0x3093) ends periodic mode: the part abandons the measurement in progress and returns to single shot mode within 1 ms. It is sent before any other command except Fetch Data.
If communication is lost, keep SDA high and clock SCL nine or more times, then send a START before the next command. Only the interface is reset; the status register keeps its contents.

In idle, the soft reset command 0x30A2 resets the system controller and reloads calibration data, without removing power. Calibration data is also reloaded before every measurement by default. No commands are processed while any reset is under way.

Sending 0x06 to the general call address 0x00 resets the part the same way as the nRESET pin, but every device on the bus that answers general calls resets too. It works only while the sensor can still process I2C commands. For a full reset without a power cycle, nRESET is the preferred route.
A hard reset is VDD switched off and on. SDA, SCL and ADDR must be brought down as well, so that the part is not fed through its ESD diodes.

The built-in heater is for plausibility checks only. It warms the sensor by a few degrees, the amount depending on conditions, draws 3.6 mW to 33 mW depending on supply, is switched by command (0x306D on, 0x3066 off), shows in status bit 13, and is off after any reset.
A 16-bit status word, read with 0xF32D, reports heater state, alert flags, whether a reset has happened and whether the last command and last write checksum were accepted. 0x3041 clears the flags.
Readings are unsigned 16-bit integers, already linearised and compensated; the conversion equations turn them into %RH, °C and °F.

Open-cavity DFN (dual flat no leads), with the humidity opening centred on the top. The silicon die sits on a copper lead frame plated Ni/Pd/Au, overmolded in epoxy with the centre pad and I/O pads left bare. The sawn side walls show unplated lead-frame copper. Apart from the opening the outline follows JEDEC publication 95, design registration 4.20 (QFN/SON), Issue D.01, September 2009. MSL 1 to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020; process within one year of delivery.

Laser marked on top: a pin-1 mark and the product name SHT3x, where x is the accuracy class, on the first line; six characters XYABCD on the second. XY (DI) is the output mode, A the year of manufacture (4 = 2014, 5 = 2015 and so on), BCD a tracking code only Sensirion can decode, available on justified request.

Non-solder-mask-defined pads with 60 µm to 75 µm clearance from copper to mask; at 0.5 mm pitch, one mask opening per row of four I/O pads. Stencil: laser-cut stainless steel, electropolished trapezoidal walls, 0.1 mm or 0.125 mm thick. I/O apertures are as long as the pads but moved 0.1 mm outward from the package centre. The centre aperture covers about 70 % to 90 % of the pad, around 0.9 mm × 1.6 mm.
Qualified to JEDEC JESD47. RoHS and WEEE compliant, free of Pb, Cd and Hg. Reels ship sealed in antistatic ESD bags.
